To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the targeting requirements of IMPs correlate with the presence of large periplasmically exposed domains and that the structure and number of transmembrane domains are also important.
the structure of multiple polypeptide domains determines the signal recognition particle targeting requirement ofEscherichiacoli inner membrane proteins.

SRP is not required for the insertion of most IMPs, that the structure of the protein, not just the presence of an N-terminal targeting signal, determines SRP dependence, and that the SRP dependence of the insertion of an AcrB- alkaline phosphatase (AP) hybrid protein correlates with the presence of an extended periplasmic loop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the signal recognition particle (srp) pathway.
the biogenesis of integral inner membrane proteins (IMP).
the molecular mechanisms of protein translocation into the Escherchia coli cell envelope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the targeting requirements of a protein are determined by its structure and the structure of both the periplasmic and membrane-spanned domains of a protein determine the degree to which it is SRP dependent for efficient insertion.
SRP is a general and necessary component for the insertion of polytopic proteins into the inner membrane, and it is not required for the insertion of bitopic membrane proteins.
the SRP is a general targeting pathway for all proteins, but it is not a necessary one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the targeting requirements of an IMP correlate with the number of transmembrane domains and the size of the periplasmic domains.
the SRP targeting pathway is required to efficiently insert a large number of polytopic IMPs into the inner membrane of E. coli. However
the structure of the multiple polypeptide domains determines the SRP targeting requirement ofEscherichiacoli inner membrane proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple pathways to the membrane and the structure of the protein dictates which one is used.
the structure of the entire protein determines its targeting pathway.
the targeting requirement of a protein is determined by its structure, not its function.
